title: network.IDN_show_punycode stopped working
body: I set network.IDN_show_punycode to true in about:config, but visiting https://www.xn--80ak6aa92e.com still shows the URL bar as apple.com instead of the punycode form. Tested on Firefox 130.0b4 64-bit on Windows; Firefox Developer for Android is affected too. This pref is how I protect myself from IDN homograph phishing (Chrome alerts about such domains natively; Firefox does not). Screen recording attached. Please tell me how I can show punycode for dangerous lookalike domains again.

symptoms_visible: With network.IDN_show_punycode=true, homograph domains (e.g. xn--80ak6aa92e.com) still display in their lookalike unicode form in the URL bar, on desktop 130.0b4 and Firefox Developer for Android; Firefox 131 is affected as well.
No alert or punycode display distinguishes the lookalike from the real site.
N0.label: N0 pref ineffective reported

symptoms_visible: Bug was closed as a duplicate of the general whole-script-confusable handling, but the pref remains non-functional; reporter reopens the complaint: 'the bug has been flagged as resolved but is not'.
N1_x.label: N1_x duplicate-dismissal aftermath

symptoms_visible: Pref remains non-functional; the change that broke it has been localized to the IDN rework push range.
N2.label: N2 regressor windowed

symptoms_visible: The recommended punycode-detection extension flags only a few domains and does not solve the reporter's cases; on Android the reporter cannot install such extensions at all, so the situation is unchanged there.
N3_x.label: N3_x extension-recommendation aftermath

symptoms_visible: Pref remains non-functional; the reporter's reliance on it and the absence of workable alternatives on Android are established.
N4.label: N4 restore decision ready

symptoms_visible: After updating to a Nightly containing the restored pref, flipping network.IDN_show_punycode=true shows homograph domains in punycode form in the URL bar, on desktop first and on Android Nightly a few days later.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Close the report as a duplicate of the general whole-script-confusable IDN display policy — treat the behavior as working as intended.
solution.concrete_example: This is the whole-script confusable case; marking as duplicate of the existing IDN display bug.

edges.comment: Real thread c4/c7-c9: duplicate-of-1332714 dismissal; the reporter's actual complaint (pref no longer honored) was untouched, so the case reopened.

question_patterns: Can we narrow down when the pref stopped working — could you (or a triager) bisect with network.IDN_show_punycode=true?
Which release first shows the pref being ignored?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Regression window with network.IDN_show_punycode=true: the autoland pushlog range containing the IDN display rework — the pref path was removed there (later cleanup removed the dangling pref definition).

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Bisection shows the pref still works in a clean profile at every build; only the reporter's profile ignores it (broken user.js overrides the value).
Same pushlog window, reported by a different volunteer a day later.

edges.comment: Real thread c5-c6: volunteer triager supplied the window; a contributor identified the removal as an intentional consequence of the IDN rework (engineer-side reading recorded as the extra info gain on N2).

solution.intent: Recommend a third-party punycode-detection extension as the replacement, noting broader IDN spoofing improvements shipping in the next release.
solution.concrete_example: Install the punycode-domain-detection add-on; IDN spoofing improvements ship in Firefox 131 and the cyrillic lookalike fix is tracked separately.

edges.comment: Real thread c13-c15: the extension flags only a few domains and cannot be installed on Android; the reporter rejected it and the second duplicate-closure was reverted.

question_patterns: How were you using this pref — do you depend on it day to day, and would an extension work for you?
It would help to know how many people used this hidden pref and whether alternatives are viable for your setup.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Security guides recommend enabling it manually since Firefox shows no alert (Chrome does natively). On Android, stable Firefox has no about:config and the two punycode extensions cannot be installed, so the pref is the only protection there; wants the manual setting back.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The extension actually covers all the reporter's cases including Android, and the reporter is satisfied using it.

edges.comment: Real thread c10-c12: the maintainer explicitly wanted usage evidence before deciding whether to re-implement the pref; the reporter's answer motivated restoring it.

solution.intent: Restore the network.IDN_show_punycode pref (pref-bound early return in the IDN safety check), land it, and guide verification: retest after the next Nightly update on desktop, then on Android Nightly once it picks up the change.
solution.concrete_example: Patch 'Restore the network.IDN_show_punycode pref' lands on autoland; Nightly updates twice a day, so retest after the next update — desktop verified first, Android Nightly picks it up a few days later; beta uplift requested.

edges.comment: Resolution per c16-c43: pref restored; premature verification (tested 1h after landing) resolved by explaining the twice-daily Nightly cadence; QA verified on Windows and Ubuntu; beta uplift followed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify that the pref stopped working because the IDN display rework intentionally removed its code path (later cleanup deleted the pref definition) — not user error, not a per-site issue.

Must not resolve by dismissal: closing as duplicate of generic homograph handling and recommending the third-party extension are both falsified in this case (extension covers few domains and is unavailable on Android).

The resolution must restore an opt-in punycode display equivalent to the old pref, covering desktop and Android, with verification guidance that accounts for the Nightly update cadence (a build from before the landing cannot show the fix).
Must treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter confirms on an updated build.

persona_hint.experience_level: Non-expert security-conscious end user; can edit about:config by following guides but misreads release/update mechanics (tested a build from before the fix landed).
persona_hint.communication_style: Anxious and persistent; repeats the core complaint when feeling dismissed; imperfect English; effusive gratitude once helped; apologizes for earlier pressure.
